Remark
[local models under rescaling]

Source: petersen:page-0454 ↗ def:pet-ch11-cmalpha-norm-global ↗ thm:pet-ch11-fundamental-theorem-convergence 1. ch11:11.6.10Define the local models of a Riemannian class to be limits obtained by rescaling elements of the class by constants $\to \infty $; e.g. $|\sec |\le K$ rescales to $|\sec |\le \lambda ^{-2}K\to 0$, so the local models are the flat manifolds, and adding $\inj \ge R$ forces $\inj \to \infty $ under rescaling, so the only local model is Euclidean space. Show that a class of spaces is compact in the $C^{m,\alpha }$ topology if every sequence in the class, rescaled by constants $\to \infty $, subconverges in $C^{m,\alpha }$ to Euclidean space.
